findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot handle datetime order_by used by audit logs
findings.body: The audit-log endpoint selects `OptimizedCursorPaginator` with `order_by="-datetime"` (organization_auditlogs.py:79), but this class reuses `BasePaginator` numeric key handling instead of `DateTimePaginator`'s datetime conversion. `get_item_key` calls `math.floor(value)` / `math.ceil(value)` on the `AuditLogEntry.datetime` value, which raises `TypeError: must be real number, not datetime` while `build_cursor` constructs cursors, so the first request with `optimized_pagination=true` returns 500. Additionally, `value_from_cursor` returns `cursor.value` unchanged, so pagination would pass an integer cursor value into `build_queryset`'s datetime `<=` filter, producing an invalid or incorrect query. The optimized path needs the same datetime-to-int and int-to-datetime conversions as `DateTimePaginator`.

findings.title: Negative-offset advanced path passes negative slices to Django QuerySet
findings.body: When `enable_advanced_features` is true and `cursor.offset < 0`, `get_result` calls `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative `start_offset`. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexes; this raises `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported.` rather than returning data. Cursor offsets are parsed from user-supplied cursor strings by `Cursor.from_string` and are not validated, so an authorized user of the optimized path can trigger a 500, and the advertised reverse-pagination feature never works. Validate/reject negative offsets or translate them into a supported query plan instead of passing them to ORM slicing.

findings.title: New optimized pagination path has no tests
findings.body: No tests were added for `OptimizedCursorPaginator`, the new `optimized_pagination` branch, or the authorization gate in `organization_auditlogs.py`. Basic coverage of first-page fetches, forward/backward cursors, datetime keys, negative offsets, and the non-admin fallback would have caught both the datetime `TypeError` and the negative-slicing `ValueError` in this PR.
